topic: CRM myths: spreadsheet is enough; CRMs are for big firms

image_defaults.prompt_suffix: Visual style: calm, precise, premium, quiet confidence. A matte near-black ground (#121515) with fine film grain, lit by one soft warm brass-toned light source. Palette: near-black, mist white (#F4F9F9), deep ink-blue (#0C2027), warm brass tones and at most ONE small gold (#F5C13A) accent. Large areas of deliberate empty negative space so text can be placed on top later. Flat, restrained, editorial. Avoid: neon, lens flare, glossy 3D blobs, cyber grids, circuit boards, rockets, light bulbs, handshakes, stock-photo people, faces, hands, fake UI, charts, and any text, letters, numbers, logos or watermarks in the image.

assets.prompt: A closed matte black ledger notebook with a plain cover and a brass pen lying beside it on a dark desk, one small brass paperclip on the cover, warm brass light from the upper left. Everything sits in the lower half of the frame; the upper 45% is empty ground. Shot straight from above. No printed or written text anywhere.

slides.title: Myth: a spreadsheet is enough.
slides.lead: It looks tidy at ten leads. At fifty, nobody knows who is next.

slides.title: Fact: you need a next step.
slides.lead: A CRM shows who to contact next. A sheet only stores names.

slides.title: Myth: CRMs are for big firms.
slides.lead: Small teams lose the most when a lead goes quiet.

slides.title: Fact: simple is the point.
slides.lead: Start with who they are, what happens next and what it is worth.

caption:
Two CRM myths, busted.

A spreadsheet stores names. A CRM shows who to contact next. And small teams lose the most when a lead goes quiet.

We're building a simple one. Follow along.

#crm #smallbusiness #customerrelationships #businesstips #aerelo
